Gram-Schmidt: k loop sequential. Parallelize i loops with reductions, and j loop. Use single parallel region per k? Simplest: parallelize inner i loops with omp for reduction for nrm, and j loop parallel.

Write:

for k:
  nrm = 0; #pragma omp parallel { ... } — use one parallel region per k containing three for loops with barriers.

#pragma omp parallel
{
  #pragma omp for reduction(+:nrm)
  for i nrm += ...
  #pragma omp for
  for i Q[i][k]=A[i][k]/R[k][k];  // R[k][k] read — needs barrier after previous loop, implicit barrier ok.
  #pragma omp for
  for j... { R[k][j]=0; for i R[k][j]+=...; for i A[i][j]-=...; }
}

nrm must be shared reduction — declared outside parallel, reduction works. R[k][k] computed before region? nrm reduction completes at barrier, but R[k][k]=sqrt(nrm) must be done by single thread then barrier before Q loop. Do:

#pragma omp parallel
{
  #pragma omp for reduction(+:nrm)
  ...
  #pragma omp single
  R[k][k] = sqrt(nrm);
  #pragma omp for
  Q loop
  #pragma omp for
  j loop
}

That's fine.
